metadata.title: Companion stars of Type Ia supernovae and hypervelocity stars

evidence.quote: US 708 is an extremely He-rich sdO star in the Galaxy halo
HVSs are stars with a velocity so great that they are able to escape the gravitational pull of the Galaxy.
At present, only one HVS, US 708, is a subdwarf O (sdO) star
whether HVSs such as US 708 could have been released from the binaries that produced SNe Ia
Thus, a surviving companion star in the WD + He star channel may have a high velocity like US 708

values.condition: Heliocentric radial velocity reported for US 708 (from Hirsch et al. 2005).

evidence.quote: US 708 is an extremely He-rich sdO star in the Galaxy halo, with a heliocentric radial velocity of+ 7 0 8 \pm 1 5 \mathrm { k m / s }(Hirsch et al. 2005).

notes: US 708: classified as follow_up rather than a newly found candidate because the paper adopts its prior HVS status—an HVS being defined as able to escape the Galaxy—and examines whether a WD + He star SN Ia companion could reproduce its high velocity (T:p1-b13, T:p2-b1, T:p4-b0). No Gaia identifier is supplied. HE 0437-5439 appears only in the introductory HVS census (T:p1-b13) and is not analyzed, so it is not rostered.
